name: Cross-origin suite: CSRF -> clickjacking -> CSWSH -> cookie scope
goal: Assemble the victim-side action surface: state changes without CSRF, clickjacking, cross-origin WebSocket, and overbroad cookie scope.
impact: Unauthorized actions on behalf of logged-in users; cookie fixation from sibling origins.

steps.purpose: Prove a state change succeeds without any token — the core CSRF primitive.
steps.on_success: Pick the highest-value state change (email/password/admin) for the PoC.
steps.on_fail: Token enforced -> SameSite/Referer gaps and login-CSRF variants (documented).

steps.purpose: UI redress completes the browser attack surface where token/origin checks are weak.
steps.on_fail: Framing blocked -> keep CSRF evidence; try WS next.

steps.purpose: CSWSH: attacker page opens authenticated WS and issues actions as the victim.
steps.on_success: WS actions on behalf of victims — strong modern CSRF analog.
steps.on_fail: Origin checked -> keep as hardening finding; CSRF alone stands.

steps.purpose: Overbroad Domain cookies make sibling-subdomain attacks (cookie injection/fixation) land.
steps.on_success: Fixation story: attacker sets cookie on any sibling, victim submits it.
steps.on_fail: Scope tight -> document suite without fixation.

entry_points: WebSocket endpoints (grep JS for new WebSocket)

recon.name: Token presence census
recon.how: Inventory which forms carry CSRF tokens; the missing ones are the proof set.

recon.name: SameSite audit
recon.how: Inspect Set-Cookie attributes: SameSite=None without Secure, or legacy Lax bypass via subdomains.

recon.name: Frame options check
recon.how: X-Frame-Options/CSP frame-ancestors absence on action pages.

recon.name: WS origin test
recon.how: Open WS from a foreign origin with victim cookies (cookie-authenticated WS = CSWSH).

recon.name: Cookie scope map
recon.how: Collect Domain attributes; overbroad scope + attacker-controllable sibling = fixation vector.

pivot_hints: combine with oauth chain for silent account binding
cookie fixation pairs with takeover chains
